'''Joan Mary''' "'''Jan'''" '''Anderson''' [[Australian Academy of Science|FAA]]  [[Royal Society|FRS]] (13 May 1932 – 28 August 2015) was a New Zealand scientist who worked in [[Canberra]], Australia, distinguished by her investigation of [[photosynthesis]].

== Life ==
Joan Mary Anderson was born in 1932 in [[Queenstown, New Zealand|Queenstown]], New Zealand. Her father [[William Anderson (New Zealand politician)|Dr Bill Anderson]] was a country doctor. Her mother died, after a long illness, when Anderson was eight.<ref name="Women Scientists">{{cite book| title=Profiles: Australian Women Scientists|first=Ragbir|last=Bhathal|author-link=Ragbir Bhathal|year=1999|isbn=9780642107015|publisher=[[National Library of Australia]]|location=Canberra|pages=15–25}}</ref> After high school, Anderson decided to study organic chemistry at the [[University of Otago]]. At the time, degrees were issued by the [[University of New Zealand]], and she obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] and [[Master of Science|MSc]] with first class honours.<ref name="Women Scientists"/>

She obtained a scholarship, the King George V Memorial Fellowship for New Zealand, that allowed her to undertake postgraduate studies in the United States for one year. When she arrived at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], she found that her New Zealand postgraduate degree was not recognised, which denied her access to the library, research facilities, and health insurance. To overcome this problem, she enrolled for a PhD, which she studied towards at the [[UC Berkeley College of Chemistry]] (1956–59) under the supervision of [[Melvin Calvin]]; Calvin received the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] in 1961.<ref name="ANU obit">{{cite web |date=1 September 2015 |title=Vale Jan Anderson |url=http://biology.anu.edu.au/news-events/vale-jan-anderson |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170530195628/http://biology.anu.edu.au/news-events/vale-jan-anderson |archive-date=30 May 2017 |access-date=21 January 2018 |publisher=Australian National University}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Melvin Calvin - Facts |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/1961/calvin-facts.html |website= Nobelprize.org |publisher=Nobel Media |access-date=6 February 2016}}</ref>

She then taught at [[Wellington Girls' College|Wellington Girls' High School]] under a bond, but broke this arrangement to take up a job offer with the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] (CSIRO) made to her four years earlier by John Falk of CSIRO Plant Industry.<ref name="ANU obit"/>

She was the first to show that the photosynthetic mechanism comprises two fundamental components: photosystem I and photosystem II.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org/page.asp?id=1475 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080609103512/http://royalsociety.org/page.asp?id=1475 |archive-date=9 June 2008 |title=Professor Jan Anderson FRS - Shedding light on photosynthesis |publisher=[[Royal Society]] }}</ref> Anderson was an adjunct professor at the [[Australian National University]].<ref name="ANU obit"/>

Anderson died on 28 August 2015.<ref name="ANU obit"/> Her funeral was held at [[St John the Baptist Church, Reid]], Canberra.<ref>{{cite web |title=Joan (Jan) Mary Anderson |url=https://www.heavenaddress.com/obituaries/funeral-notice/Joan-Jan-Mary-ANDERSON/1134862 |work=Obituary |publisher=HeavenAddress |access-date=6 February 2016 |archive-date=10 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230310162637/https://www.heavenaddress.com/obituaries/funeral-notice/Joan-Jan-Mary-ANDERSON/1134862 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
She received many honors and awards for her work, including the [[Lemberg Medal]] in 1983,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lemberg Medal Winners |url=https://www.asbmb.org.au/lemberg-medal-winners |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=Australian Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology}}</ref> election as a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 1987, and as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anderson, Jan profile |publisher=Encyclopedia of Australian Science |date=7 February 2011 |first=Annette |last=Alafaci |url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004441b.htm |access-date=7 February 2016 }}</ref><ref>Horton, Peter; Soon Chow, Wah; Barret, Christopher (2018). "Joan Mary Anderson. 12 May 1932—28 August 2015". ''[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]''. [https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2018.0006 doi.org/10.1098/rsbm.2018.0006].</ref> She was awarded an honorary doctorate from [[Umeå University]] in 1998. She was awarded the [[Centenary Medal]] in 2001.<ref name="ANU obit"/> In 2017, she was selected as one of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand's]] "[[150 women in 150 words]]".<ref name="royalsociety">{{cite web |title=150 Women in 150 Words |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/ |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi |access-date=11 November 2020}}</ref>
